key_insight: Matrix-structured optimizers, especially SOAP and SOAP-Muon, can train ML interatomic potentials faster and to better accuracy than Adam, making optimizer choice a major lever for performance.
engineering_relevance: For practical MLIP development, switching optimizers may improve both training efficiency and label efficiency, especially when force labels are partially available.
method: Compared Adam against Muon, SOAP, and SOAP-Muon.
Trained NequIP and Allegro MLIP models under the same benchmark setting.
Evaluated convergence speed and final accuracy, including partial force supervision cases.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic comparisons showing that SOAP and SOAP-Muon consistently outperform Adam, with the largest gains under partial force supervision.
watch_item: These gains may depend on model architecture, training setup, and the extra implementation complexity of matrix-structured optimizers.
paper_title: Beyond Adam: SOAP and Muon for Faster, Label-Efficient Training of Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
